messages.subject: BioGeoBEARS issues: Windows machines, small trees
parts:
Hi group -- some recent answers, post-optimx fix:


Hi again! OK, I have a moment now... actually, do you mind if I post
these answers to the BioGeoBEARS google group?  This will help others
who have the same issue.


On Thu, Jan 16, 2014 at 12:52 AM,  X wrote:
> Dr. Matzke,
> I'm running BioGeoBEARS (pretty much that "out of the box" example with my
> data).
>
> I have a couple of questions:
>
>
> I'm getting quite different likelihoods if I run with "use_optimx=T" or "F".
> Something like -630 (when false) versus -920 (true). Do you have any idea
> about what might be going on?

This indicates the two Maximum Likelihood search optimizations are
finding different solutions.  I typically prefer optimx as it is
faster, but they should converge on the same result.  If the search is
hitting the limits of the parameters, though, then the search will
never find the optimum.  Hopefully, this will go away when the default
maximum values are adjusted, as below.


> The default maximum values for "d" and "e" are 5. I have to increase that a
> lot... I'm getting something like d=150, e=49. Should I be worried?? My tree
> has 120 tips and 8 areas.

This is fine.  It does mean that you probably have a very "short"
tree, with tiny branch lengths.  If you multiplied all of your
branches by 100 and saved this to a new Newick file, you would find that your optimal d and e parameters would then be 100 times smaller.

So, you can either rescale your tree, or raise the maximum value of d and e.  d and e are just
the "rate of the event per unit branch length", typically 5 is a good
max for a tree with a depth of 1 to 100, and units of millions of
years, but if you have a short tree you can change it.

(This logic only applies to the anagenetic parameters, not the
cladogenetic parameters.)


> As I said, I'm running the example. The first 5 models ran Ok (after I
> increased the maximum value), but the BAYAREAj is giving me an error:
>
> Error in calc_loglike_sp(tip_condlikes_of_data_on_each_state =
> tip_condlikes_of_data_on_each_state,  :
>   number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length
> However, it works if I run with use_optimx=T. Any idea?


This might mean that optim() is trying some value that produces a NaN
likelihood.  You could try adjusting the min/max values on the
parameters so that they are slightly further from 0 or 1 -- sometimes
the optimization seems to try values that are slightly beyond the
limits, even though I've set limits. Sometimes making the limits
tighter fixes things.

But, if it works with optimx, just use optimx.

Strangely, the error on the BayArea+J optimization run seems to happen only on Windows machines.  It may be some slight difference in how small numbers are treated, and some parameter value that is being tried during the search, that should be slightly above zero, is being rounded to 0 or a negative value.  This might be fixable by fiddling with the min for the variable parameters.


> If I use the source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--...... )  and more than
> one core, it gives me an error "cannot find detectCore function". With one
> core works fine.

For this, do
install.packages("parallel")
library(parallel)

...the newer versions of R come with parallel as a default, but
apparently this is not the case with Windows versions. Or, as you
found, just use one core.

Cheers!
